title: Making game assets for $0: how far can free AI 3D tools get you?
author: Head-Buy4008
selftext:
I've been looking into free AI 3D options for making a few custom props in Unity. The generation credits are nice but I'm more interested in what happens after u get the model.  
Meshy gives you 100 credits each month and 10 downloads of untextured Meshy 6 Lite models. They're under CC BY 4.0, so commercial use is possible with attribution. For simple props, that could work.  you'd still need to take them through Blender, sort out materials and UVs and get everything into Unity  
Tripo has 200 monthly credits, with free exports limited to H2.5. I'd be careful with the licensing before including anything in a commercial release..  
Then there's the open source route. No monthly credit allowance to worry abt, but you need the hardware to run it and texturing or cleaning up the results is still your job.  
A handful of custom static props on a $0 budget seems doable. Trying to build a whole cast of textured, rigged, animated characters for free is another level of work.  
Free generation helps, but there's still a fair bit of actual game art to do afterward.

comments.author: Hotwingz66
comments.body:
[https://3d.hunyuan.tencent.com/creation](https://3d.hunyuan.tencent.com/creation)

There is also a local version you can check out if you have the gpu for it.  
You can certainly have gpt or whatever check it out for you.

My answer after having started free is, you can get some first steps done for free.  
But if you discover that you are serious enough with achieving your goal then 20 to 40 dollars can get your foot in the door. Limit your expectations accordingly.

However, if you take the effort to rig and animate etc etc yourself you can also knock down the cost.   
If you cant code or do anything art wise, you'll have to budget for it. 

Good Luck.
